title: Microsoft Earnings Beat Estimates as Revenue Rises 19% to $92.3 Billion and Azure Jumps 48%
excerpt: Microsoft's fiscal first quarter topped Wall Street estimates on accelerating Azure growth, a $677 billion booked backlog and free cash flow that stayed strongly positive despite $45.2 billion of AI capital spending.
body:
• Microsoft beat estimates on both lines for its fiscal first quarter: revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion against about $90.7 billion expected, and adjusted earnings were $4.89 per share against $4.73 expected.
  • Azure revenue jumped 48% to $33.17 billion, ahead of estimates, and Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9 billion — demand for AI infrastructure is converting into reported sales, not just bookings.
  • Guidance points higher: second-quarter revenue of $96 billion to $97.1 billion, Azure growth of 49% to 50% in constant currency, and capital spending above $50 billion in the quarter as Microsoft races to add capacity.
  • Cash held up better than at rivals: free cash flow was $18.6 billion despite $45.2 billion of capital spending, and Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in the quarter.

Microsoft opened its fiscal year with a clean beat on Wednesday, as accelerating cloud growth showed its heavy artificial intelligence spending producing revenue faster than Wall Street expected. The company reported revenue of $92.3 billion for the quarter ended September 30, up 19% from a year earlier, with operating income up 21% to $45.9 billion.

Azure does the heavy lifting

Net income was $36.6 billion on a GAAP basis, up 32%, and $36.4 billion on an adjusted basis that excludes the impact of Microsoft's investments in OpenAI. Diluted earnings per share were $4.92 on a GAAP basis and $4.89 adjusted, up 18% adjusted and ahead of the $4.73 consensus.

https://x.com/Microsoft/status/2115535611801248094

The engine was Azure. Reuters reported Azure revenue grew 48% to $33.17 billion, topping the $32.84 billion Visible Alpha estimate and accelerating from $29.4 billion in the prior quarter. Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9 billion, up 30%, and commercial remaining performance obligation — work booked but not yet billed — surged 73% to $677 billion, a backlog that underwrites future quarters.

"We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% year-over-year. Results exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income, and earnings per share."

— Amy Hood, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Microsoft

Chairman and chief executive Satya Nadella said the company is "delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack," pointing to adoption of Copilot and its Foundry platform for building AI agents. On the earnings call, management said Copilot daily users grew nearly 50% quarter over quarter, Foundry revenue more than tripled, and Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue rose 18% on an adjusted basis to $27.8 billion.

The rest of the portfolio was mixed

Under Microsoft's recast segments, Agents and Infra revenue was $76.8 billion, up 25%, while Devices and Consumer revenue fell 3% to $15.5 billion. Search and advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs rose 12% on higher volume and rates across Bing and Edge. Xbox content and services revenue slipped 2% on weaker third-party content and Game Pass subscriptions, and Windows OEM and devices revenue fell sharply as partners drew down inventory amid weaker PC demand — a soft spot management flagged explicitly on the call.

Spending is large, but cash flow stayed positive

Capital expenditure was $45.2 billion in the quarter, up from $34.9 billion a year earlier but below Microsoft's own $50 billion projection, after some third-party capacity deliveries were delayed. Free cash flow was $18.6 billion, well ahead of the $8.54 billion analysts expected according to Visible Alpha — a contrast with Alphabet, which swung to negative free cash flow the same evening. Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks.

What comes next

For the second quarter, Microsoft guided to revenue of $96 billion to $97.1 billion, growth of 18% to 19%, with Azure growth of 49% to 50% in constant currency. Management expects capital spending to exceed $50 billion in the second quarter and to total about $170 billion for calendar 2026, while still remaining free-cash-flow positive for fiscal 2027. Shares rose about 4% in extended trading. The question for the next quarter is capacity: demand, by management's own account, still exceeds supply, so the pace of data-center delivery — not demand — sets the growth rate.
